stem:
A 32-year-old has a routine Cervical Screening Test. She is up to date with screening, immunocompetent and has no symptoms. An oncogenic HPV type other than 16 or 18 is detected, and reflex liquid-based cytology shows no abnormality.

What is the next step?

options.label: A
options.text: Colposcopy now, as an oncogenic HPV type has been found
options.explanation: Only HPV 16 or 18 goes straight to colposcopy whatever the cytology shows. For other oncogenic types the reflex cytology decides, and normal cytology does not need colposcopy now.

options.label: B
options.text: Return to routine five-yearly screening, as cytology is normal
options.explanation: A detected oncogenic HPV type needs follow-up even with normal cytology; it does not return her to the five-yearly interval.

options.label: C
options.text: Repeat cytology alone in six months, then colposcopy if abnormal
options.explanation: The pathway follows HPV (not 16/18) with a repeat HPV test, not cytology alone, and the interval is 12 months.

options.label: D
options.text: Repeat HPV testing in three years, as her cytology is normal
options.explanation: Three years is not the interval in this pathway; she is retested at 12 months to see whether the infection has cleared.

options.label: E
options.text: Repeat HPV testing in 12 months, without colposcopy now
options.explanation: HPV (not 16/18) with negative cytology in an on-time, immunocompetent screener is followed with a repeat HPV test in 12 months, because many of these infections clear in that time.

context: Oncogenic HPV other than 16 or 18, with negative cytology, is a 12-month follow-up, not immediate colposcopy.
